title: A Question with No Audience
fact_notes: オリジナル論説・架空の教育事例。実在の調査・教育効果の実証ではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: People sometimes develop an explanation of their beliefs while attempting to communicate those beliefs to someone else.
sentences.ja: 人は時に自分の信念を他者に伝えようとする過程でその説明を発展させる。

sentences.en: The expectation of an audience may encourage a speaker to notice missing details, anticipate possible objections, and arrange ideas in a more coherent order.
sentences.ja: 聴衆を想定すると話し手は不足する詳細に気づき、反論を予想し、考えをより一貫した順序に整理するよう促され得る。

sentences.en: Yet the same expectation may create a desire to defend a conclusion that has already been publicly expressed, even when the speaker has encountered information that might justify reconsidering it.
sentences.ja: しかし同じ期待が、再考を正当化し得る情報に出会ってもすでに公に述べた結論を守りたい願いを生むことがある。

sentences.en: The relationship between expressing a judgment and examining a judgment is therefore more complicated than it might initially appear.
sentences.ja: そこで判断を表明することと吟味することの関係は当初見えるより複雑だ。

sentences.en: Imagine two students who have been asked to prepare opposing arguments about a fictional proposal to change the schedule of school activities.
sentences.ja: 学校活動の日程を変更する架空提案に賛否の論拠を準備するよう頼まれた二人の生徒を想像しよう。

sentences.en: Before the debate, each student collects examples that might strengthen the position assigned to them and identifies weaknesses in the arguments they expect the other person to present.
sentences.ja: 討論前に各自は割り当てられた立場を強化し得る例を集め、相手が示すと予想する論拠の弱点を特定する。

sentences.en: The preparation provides valuable opportunities to practice explaining reasons, distinguishing relevant information from irrelevant details, and responding to alternative interpretations.
sentences.ja: 準備は理由の説明、関連情報と無関係な詳細の区別、別解釈への対応を練習する価値ある機会を提供する。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, neither student has been explicitly asked to identify the conditions under which they would be willing to abandon their assigned position.
sentences.ja: それでもどちらも割り当てられた立場を放棄する意向を持つ条件を特定するよう明示的には頼まれていない。

sentences.en: After the debate, the teacher introduces a separate writing activity in which students are not required to defend either side of the original proposal.
sentences.ja: 討論後教師は原提案のどちら側も擁護する必要のない別作文活動を導入する。

sentences.en: Each student is invited to describe a question whose answer could reasonably alter their own assessment of the proposal, then explain why that answer would matter.
sentences.ja: 各自は答えが自身の提案評価を合理的に変え得る問いを記述し、その答えが重要な理由を説明するよう促される。

sentences.en: A student who originally argued in favor of the change might identify a circumstance in which the proposed schedule would create a serious difficulty for a group of participants.
sentences.ja: 当初変更に賛成した生徒は提案日程が参加者集団に重大な困難を生む事情を特定するかもしれない。

sentences.en: A student who opposed the proposal might consider information that would demonstrate how one of the anticipated difficulties could be addressed without abandoning the entire plan.
sentences.ja: 反対した生徒は予想された困難の一つが計画全体を放棄せずに解決できることを示す情報を考えるかもしれない。

sentences.en: The activity emphasizes the difference between identifying a weakness in someone else's argument and identifying a possible limitation of one's own judgment.
sentences.ja: 活動は他者の論拠の弱点特定と自身の判断の可能な限界の特定との違いを強調する。

sentences.en: The fictional teacher does not assume that completing such an activity will automatically make students more open to every opposing opinion.
sentences.ja: 架空教師は活動完了が自動的に生徒を全反対意見に寛容にするとは想定しない。

sentences.en: Nor does the exercise require participants to change their positions merely to demonstrate a willingness to reconsider them.
sentences.ja: また活動は再考への意欲を示すだけのために立場変更を要求しない。

sentences.en: A belief may remain reasonable after alternatives have been examined, and maintaining a position can be justified when the available evidence continues to support it.
sentences.ja: 別案を吟味しても信念は合理的なままであり得て、利用可能証拠が支持し続けるなら立場維持は正当化され得る。

sentences.en: What matters in the exercise is whether students can distinguish evidence that would genuinely affect their reasoning from information that merely helps them present their existing position more persuasively.
sentences.ja: 活動で重要なのは推論に本当に影響する証拠と既存立場をより説得的に提示するだけの情報の区別ができるかだ。

sentences.en: Learning to argue effectively and learning to revise one's judgments can be complementary objectives without being identical activities.
sentences.ja: 効果的論証を学ぶことと判断修正を学ぶことは同一活動でなくても相補的目的になり得る。

sentences.en: The former involves communicating the reasons for a position, while the latter involves examining the conditions under which those reasons would no longer be sufficient.
sentences.ja: 前者は立場の理由を伝えることを伴い、後者はその理由がもはや十分でなくなる条件を検討することを伴う。

sentences.en: A person need not abandon a carefully considered belief in order to acknowledge that further information could change its justification.
sentences.ja: 追加情報が信念の正当化を変え得ると認めるために慎重に考えた信念を放棄する必要はない。

sentences.en: The question with no audience becomes a reminder that reasoning can serve the purpose of inquiry as well as persuasion.
sentences.ja: 誰にも見せない問いは推論が説得だけでなく探究の目的も果たすことを思い出させる。

connected in a clear and logical way
give reasons in favor of something

in a manner likely to convince
act of causing someone to accept a view

questions.prompt: What tension does the opening identify?
options: An audience prevents speakers from organizing thoughts.
Public expressions always reflect a person's complete reasoning.
Beliefs cannot be communicated to any audience.
An audience can improve an explanation while also encouraging defense of an existing conclusion.
questions.explanation_ja: 説明の改善と立場防衛の両面。

questions.prompt: What might justify reconsideration of a belief?
options: The existence of an audience alone.
New information encountered by the speaker.
The number of words in a speech.
A requirement to abandon all beliefs.

questions.prompt: What do students prepare before the debate?
options: A list of conditions requiring them to change positions.
A final decision accepted by both sides.
Examples and responses supporting assigned positions.
A report on actual school policy.
questions.explanation_ja: 割り当てられた立場の論証。

questions.prompt: What has not been emphasized in debate preparation?
options: Conditions under which one's own position might reasonably change.
How to identify relevant information.
How to explain reasons.
How to anticipate opposing arguments.
questions.explanation_ja: 自分の立場の変更条件。

questions.prompt: What is the separate writing activity about?
options: A second debate defending the same side.
A requirement to reject the entire proposal.
An evaluation of classmates' speaking voices.
A question whose answer could alter one's assessment.

questions.prompt: Why might a student who opposes the change examine possible solutions?
options: They must support every possible change.
They can consider whether an objection is decisive or can be addressed.
They are forbidden to consider their earlier reasons.
They have to accept the other student's conclusions.
questions.explanation_ja: 反対理由が解決できるか検討する。

questions.prompt: Why does the teacher not require a change of position?
options: Reconsideration can still support the original judgment.
Every belief becomes unreasonable after discussion.
The goal is to reject all evidence.
Participants must maintain the same view forever.
questions.explanation_ja: 再検討後も立場は合理的であり得る。

questions.prompt: What distinction matters in the exercise?
options: Facts about speaking speed versus facts about writing speed.
The teacher's opinion versus every student's identity.
Evidence affecting reasoning versus information making existing arguments more persuasive.
Arguments in one language versus another language.
questions.explanation_ja: 判断への影響と説得力の違い。

options: Learning to speak publicly.
Learning to revise one's judgments.
Learning to collect unrelated facts.
Learning to avoid discussion.
questions.explanation_ja: 後者＝判断修正を学ぶこと。

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the argument?
options: Persuasive argument and sound judgment are necessarily identical.
A reasonable person must abandon every existing belief.
Debate should never be practiced in schools.
Learning to reason involves examining what would justify revising a position as well as communicating its support.
questions.explanation_ja: 論証と再考を区別し両方学ぶ。

paraphrases.source: Yet the same expectation may create a desire to defend a conclusion that has already been publicly expressed, even when the speaker has encountered information that might justify reconsidering it.
paraphrases.rewrite: Public commitment may encourage defense of a position despite new evidence worth considering.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 公に表明した立場へのこだわり。

paraphrases.source: Nevertheless, neither student has been explicitly asked to identify the conditions under which they would be willing to abandon their assigned position.
paraphrases.rewrite: Neither student has been asked what conditions could lead them to give up their position.

paraphrases.source: Nor does the exercise require participants to change their positions merely to demonstrate a willingness to reconsider them.
paraphrases.rewrite: The task does not require a student to change their opinion just to show openness.

paraphrases.source: The former involves communicating the reasons for a position, while the latter involves examining the conditions under which those reasons would no longer be sufficient.
paraphrases.rewrite: Argument explains reasons for a stance, whereas revision examines when those reasons may cease to be sufficient.
